output.explanation:
This corrects the supplied sample while retaining its eleven batch boundaries, stable diagram identities, and scaffold positions. The batches partition all 69 commits in supplied order; b01 contains exactly first-batch.json. Small fixes, documentation, and commits with empty supplied diffs remain grouped with their architectural changes.

The reported validation error is Invalid diagram revision parent; it does not identify a failing object. The corrected execution contract is explicit: resolve each canvas/diagram pair against the actual preceding frozen state, obtain its current bound revision, and retain that revision's required ancestry before issuing or publishing a child revision. A diagram revision parent must identify the same logical diagram. Git SHAs, content-version strings, historical read-scoped aliases, and another canvas's revision are not interchangeable with that parent. Preserve existing revisionBoundary data when supported; do not fabricate boundaries, delete parent links, or reconstruct histories from ASCII. A redraw revises the existing object rather than creating a replacement identity. Fill each new scaffold by revising its actual scaffold revision. Preserve independently pinned bindings on historical roll-up canvases, even where display IDs or content are shared. Reuse retained results on uncertain retries. These are Phase 2 handoff requirements, not a claim that the unspecified runtime failure has been reproduced.

The supplied baseline revision is 03f2168deba364103c2450ca9b8168cd1fc9ddc5, whereas commit-001 names e883718ed42d4f2174e3b1a4429396a6fc5bb180 as its parent. Follow the supplied sequence and restored checkpoints without inventing an intervening change. Selected paths exist at their batch endpoints and include relevant unchanged dependencies. Future dependencies guide organization only; their functionality must not appear before its implementing batch.

C00-C06 explain implementation. C07 initially contains proposed revision/presentation designs and is reconciled as implementation arrives. C09 similarly progresses from proposed saved views to implemented recording and then branching. C08 remains an unchanged tldraw library reference. C10-C15 remain historical proposals or composite roll-ups, explicitly identified in b01. C04's SearchArtifact remains proposed. Preserve C02/D00's unused placeholder.

Preserve every existing position, relationship, and exact retainedAttachments label, including spacing and multiline labels. Superseded attachment labels remain under explicitly historical branches with current replacements nearby. Preserve new attachment labels across subsequent edits as well. Edges below describe only new relationships. Existing edits remain concise within their original rectangles; no canvas is flattened or globally relaid out.

Each new diagram has a fixed nonnegative position and an exact introductory count of nonempty concept lines. Reserve a 100-column rectangle of at least 2*targetNodes+3 rows at each specified position. These rectangles are separated from the baseline and one another. Later updates retain the same positions and concept-line budgets through consolidation. Every named attachment must occur uniquely in its diagram. Phase 2 fills these structures; this plan supplies no full diagram content.

batches.title: Native Canvas Runtime
batches.rationale: Use the required initial range. The workspace and controller remain semantic owners while tldraw takes live camera, shape, and native undo responsibilities, so patch their overview. Add application-runtime detail on C00: granular subscriptions and local anchors already warrant a separate explanation, and later routing and side panels develop it further. C08 explains library internals rather than application ownership. Correct inherited proposal status now. Establish revision-safe execution from the restored bindings and preserve ancestry when modifying both implementation and archived diagrams.
